objective: Add Microsoft Azure as the fifth provider slice (F008 P5), to the standard set by the merged AWS slice (PR #70): one provider profile module registered through the F008 S3 seam, one provider YAML with a complete fourteen-category coverage declaration, committed official excerpts with capture.json provenance, and unit + integration + coverage-config tests. Every published fact must trace to a verbatim block or a real table cell in the SAME captured document. The central product rule outranks completeness: never publish an unsupported claim that a service is free, and never omit a real free offer either.
premise_predictions_stated_before_measur: PREDICTION (before probing): Azure, like AWS and Google Cloud, publishes its per-category free-service list through a client-rendered widget, so the free-services hub will parse to headings with no accompanying prose. OUTCOME: CONFIRMED. https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/free-services/ serves 203234 bytes, ZERO <table> elements and 236 text blocks, and the free-service list is absent: the headings 'Free for your first 12 months' and '65+ always-free services with an Azure account' are served with no allowance prose beneath them.

PREDICTION: Azure will state a payment-card requirement somewhere official, making the Azure free account Z1 exactly as AWS's free plan is. OUTCOME: CONFIRMED, and it is a quotation rather than a composition: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/offers/ms-azr-0044p/ carries the heading 'Azure free account terms & conditions' and states under its own 'Payment options' heading, verbatim: 'All you need is a phone number, a credit card or a debit card (non-prepaid), and a Microsoft account or a GitHub account. Only credit cards are accepted in Hong Kong and Brazil.'

PREDICTION (the one I most expected to be WRONG, because the AWS builder's most valuable disclosed error was concluding too early that a provider never states a perpetual offer): Azure DOES state a perpetual free tier in a block of its own. OUTCOME: CONFIRMED and stronger than predicted. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/free-tier is titled 'Lifetime Free Tier - Azure Cosmos DB | Microsoft Learn' and states, in a block of its own: 'Free tier lasts indefinitely for the lifetime of the account and it comes with all the benefits and features of a regular Azure Cosmos DB account.' That satisfies rule 1 of docs/DATA_MODEL.md by quotation, so the offer is genuinely always_free.

PREDICTION: that perpetual offer will still not be Z0. OUTCOME: CONFIRMED from the SAME block that grants the allowance: 'When free tier is enabled on an account, you get the first 1000 RU/s and 25 GB of storage in the account for free. The throughput and storage consumed beyond these limits are billed at regular price.' That is automatic_billing, so Z1_BILLING_EXPOSURE. Azure independently reproduces the AWS Step Functions finding: PERPETUAL DOES NOT MEAN Z0.

PREDICTION: no Azure page will state a SAFE exhaustion behaviour for a free tier. OUTCOME: WRONG, and this is the finding that most changed the slice. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/web-sites-monitor states: 'If an app exceeds the CPU (Short), CPU (Day), or Bandwidth quota, the app is stopped until the quota resets. During this time, all incoming requests result in an HTTP 403 error.' That is a genuine non-billing stop. The App Service Free plan therefore fails Z0 on the CARD gate alone, not on exhaustion, which is a materially different reason from every other offer in this slice and is why the offer is carried rather than dropped.

PREDICTION: no Azure page will state that a card is NOT required. OUTCOME: WRONG. https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students/ publishes the bare bullet 'No credit card required'. It is carried as a published note rather than converted into requires_card=False, for the reason recorded in card_claim_not_pinned below.

why_seven_sources_over_seven_documents: AWS used six. Azure uses seven because dropping any one would omit a distinct, evidenced outcome: the credit-backed account (Z1 on a quoted card requirement), the 12-month introductory offer, the LIFETIME Cosmos DB tier (Z1 despite being perpetual), an App Service free plan whose exhaustion is genuinely SAFE and which therefore fails on the card gate alone, a Static Web Apps free plan whose commercial structure is not stated at all (the first application of docs/DATA_MODEL.md rule 3 in this repository), a DevOps free allowance that satisfies rule 2 in both legs, and the Students programme, which carries the only block in the entire sweep stating that no card is required. Every source reads its OWN document; no profile borrows a fact from another.
card_claim_not_pinned: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/free/students/ publishes 'No credit card required' as a bare list item. requires_card=False is NOT pinned to it, and the reasoning is recorded rather than assumed. The page carries TWO offers - Azure for Students and Azure for Startups - and the Startups bullet list states the opposite direction ('Spending protection-credit card required only for identity verification and services beyond credit*'). Read alone, 'No credit card required' names no offer, so pinning it would splice one offer's terms onto a page that publishes two. The favourable fact is still PUBLISHED, carried whole as a verbatim card_claim note fact, so this is a decision about the machine-readable Z0 gate and not an omission. The choice is verdict-neutral and that is checked by test: student_program is in TEMPORARY_CONDITIONAL_OFFER_TYPES, so even with requires_card=False the offer could reach Z2 at best and never Z0, and with has_paid_dependencies unknown it is UNKNOWN either way.
acceptance_criteria: AC1. Seven Azure sources over seven distinct official documents load, extract exactly one candidate each, and reproduce a byte-stable content hash from the committed fixtures with no socket opened.

AC2. Every material Z0 condition on every profile - service, offer_type, requires_card, has_paid_dependencies, exhaustion_behaviour - is a whole-block HtmlTextAssertion pinned to verbatim source text, never a table cell, and never composed across documents.

AC3. Deleting, rewording or truncating a pinned block yields assertion_not_found; duplicating one yields ambiguous_assertion; adding an UNRELATED paragraph leaves the verdict unchanged. All three are asserted, so the guards discriminate rather than reject any edit.

AC4. No Azure offer reaches Z0_TRUE_FREE under the REAL classifier, and a positive control proves the same sweep can observe a Z0. The control asserts a synthetic always_free + requires_card=False + has_paid_dependencies=False + hard_stop offer returns Z0_TRUE_FREE with no blocking conditions.

AC5. The positive control is proven LOAD-BEARING by patching the classifier so it can no longer emit Z0 and observing the control FAIL while the non-Z0 sweep still PASSES. A control that cannot fail proves nothing.

AC6. Every fixture reconciles with live in BOTH directions, enforced by the generator, which refuses to write when parsed rows or pinned blocks differ. Both directions and their counts are recorded in each capture.json.

AC7. The mutation battery records its predictions in the parametrization BEFORE running, prints the patched line, asserts each anchor matched exactly ONCE, is green at baseline, and includes false-positive controls that must NOT fire.

AC8. All fourteen coverage categories are declared. Every unknown names what was actually probed, or says plainly that it was not probed. Nothing is verified_free. No category asserts absence without evidence.
AC9. The two matrix profiles map every live row of their target table and ignore none, so a row Azure adds later rejects the document instead of vanishing from the published comparison.

AC10. Protected state is unchanged, proven by `git hash-object` blob comparison rather than `git diff --numstat`: agent-state/feature_list.json, tests/support/source_scan.py, tests/unit/test_secrets_baseline.py, apps/api/app/ingest/adapters/html.py, apps/api/app/classify/engine.py.

negative_tests: unrelated_paragraph_added -> verdict SURVIVES (the discrimination control the brief demands).
FALSE-POSITIVE CONTROLS that must NOT fire: an extra column, and whitespace/entity noise inside a mapped row label.

Deleting the Cosmos DB overage sentence must REJECT the document rather than leave a perpetual offer whose exhaustion is merely unknown, which for an always_free offer is the exact shape of a false $0 claim.
Deleting the Azure free account payment-method block must reject rather than silently produce a cardless offer.
A block Azure publishes twice, pinned deliberately, must yield ambiguous_assertion.
The pipeline cases partial and contradictory must persist ZERO candidates.
data_implications: No migration and no schema change. New rows only: one provider, seven sources, seven candidates, their evidence and their pending review items, plus fourteen provider_category_coverage rows. Zero offers, offer versions and quotas are published, which is the point of the slice.
security_privacy: All live fetching happens OUTSIDE the test suite in an owner-run generator that lives outside the repository, so CI performs zero socket operations and tests/unit/test_no_live_fetcher_in_tests.py stays green by construction. No credential material is involved. Internal package-feed hostnames must never reach a report, the PR, a commit message or any committed file.
portability: No new dependency, no new service, no provider SDK. Azure is reached only as official HTML through the existing generic HtmlDocAdapter; all provider knowledge is data in one module.
z0_risk: MAXIMAL for this slice, in both directions. Azure markets a credit-backed free account, a 12-month introductory tier, a LIFETIME service tier and several free service plans under overlapping 'free' branding, and one of them has a genuinely safe exhaustion behaviour. Overstating any of them publishes a false $0 claim; understating the Cosmos DB lifetime tier or the Students no-card statement omits a real free offer, which this brief weights as an equal defect. Every material condition is therefore a quotation or absent, and absence yields UNKNOWN.
